subject: Copywriting
title: Nudge Theory in Copy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Nudge Theory in Copy.

hook.text: Organ donation rates jumped from 12% to 99% by changing the default from opt-in to opt-out. One word flipped.

buildup.text: Thaler and Sunstein's nudge theory: small design changes guide behavior without removing choice.

discovery.text: Copy nudges include defaulting checkboxes, pre-selecting plans, and suggesting tips. The default wins 70% of the time.

twist.text: Critics call nudges paternalistic. Who decides what the 'right' default is? Designers hold invisible power.

climax.text: Ethical nudges align the default with the user's genuine interest. Save more for retirement? Default to yes.

punchline.text: Change the default, change the outcome. Nudging works.

quiz.question: What dramatically increased organ donation rates?
options: Changing the default from opt-in to opt-out

details.summary: Nudge theory suggests that small changes in how choices are presented can dramatically influence decisions. Default settings, simplified forms, and strategic option ordering are nudges that guide behavior without restricting freedom — the art of architecture that shapes choice.
details.whyItMatters: Nudges are the subtlest form of persuasion in copy. Understanding how choice architecture influences behavior helps writers design pages, forms, and processes that guide users toward desired actions naturally.
takeaways: Default options are the most powerful nudge — most people stick with defaults
Simplifying choices and reducing friction increases desired behaviors
Nudges preserve freedom of choice while shaping likely outcomes

faq.question: What is the difference between a nudge and manipulation?
faq.answer: A nudge makes the desired option easier while preserving all alternatives. Manipulation removes or obscures alternatives. Pre-checking a newsletter signup box is a nudge; hiding the unsubscribe button is manipulation. Transparency is the ethical line.

faq.question: What are common nudges in digital copy?
faq.answer: Pre-selected annual billing (default option), highlighted 'most popular' plan (social proof nudge), progress bars on forms (completion nudge), and order summaries showing savings (framing nudge). Each subtly guides the user toward the preferred action.
